item.title: Oil majors halt Strait of Hormuz shipments amid US-Iran strikes
item.description:
Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz ground to a near-halt on Saturday as oil majors and trading houses suspended crude oil, fuel, and liquefied natural gas shipments following joint US-Israeli military strikes on Iran. Tracking data showed tanker speeds dropping to near zero as shipowners pulled vessels from the waterway that carries roughly 20 percent of the world's seaborne oil trade.

Several major oil companies and leading trading firms halted shipments through the strait as Iran declared the waterway closed to navigation, according to Reuters, citing four trading sources. "Our vessels will remain stationary for a number of days," a senior executive at a prominent trading firm said. The US Navy warned against navigating in the operational zone, which encompasses the entirety of the Gulf, the Gulf of Oman, the Arabian Sea, and the Strait of Hormuz, saying it could not guarantee the safety of commercial vessels.

item.title: CIA assessed IRGC hardliners would replace Khamenei if killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes
item.description:
In the lead-up to Saturday's joint U.S. and Israeli military operation against Iran, the Central Intelligence Agency assessed that even if Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei were killed, he would most likely be succeeded by hardline figures from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps rather than reformist elements, according to a Reuters report citing two sources briefed on the intelligence.

The finding underscores a tension at the heart of President Trump's stated ambition to topple Iran's clerical establishment: the intelligence community's own analysis suggests military force alone may not produce the kind of political transformation Washington seeks.

item.title: Israel claims top Iranian commanders killed in strikes
item.description: Israeli media reported Saturday that several high-ranking Iranian officials were killed in the coordinated US-Israel military strikes on Iran, in what analysts are describing as an apparent decapitation operation targeting the Islamic Republic's top leadership. The claims, which remain disputed by Tehran, came as explosions rocked cities across Iran on February 28, 2026.

item.title: Russia condemns US-Israeli strikes on Iran, evacuates citizens
item.description:
Russia's Foreign Ministry on Saturday sharply condemned the joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran, calling them "a pre-planned and unprovoked act of armed aggression against a sovereign and independent U.N. member state" and warning the attacks risk plunging the Middle East into chaos.

In a statement posted to Telegram, the ministry accused Washington and Tel Aviv of "hiding behind" concerns about Iran's nuclear program while pursuing regime change. It warned the strikes could trigger a "humanitarian, economic and possibly radiological catastrophe" in the region, accusing the United States and Israel of "plunging the Middle East into an abyss of uncontrolled escalation".

item.title: Iran launches retaliatory strikes on US bases after joint US-Israeli assault
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the United Nations on Saturday that all American and Israeli military bases, facilities, and assets across the Middle East would be considered legitimate targets, as Iran launched retaliatory missile strikes against US installations in multiple Gulf states following a joint US-Israeli military assault on Iranian territory.

item.title: UN Security Council holds emergency session on US-Israel strikes against Iran
item.description:
The United Nations Security Council is set to convene an emergency session at 4 p.m. EST Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes against Iran earlier in the day, plunging the Middle East into a new armed conflict. Iran has retaliated with missile and drone attacks targeting Israeli and U.S. military installations across the region, including in Jordan, Syria, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

The emergency meeting was requested by France, Russia, China, Bahrain, and Colombia, according to Reuters. Russia's UN mission said it called the session "in response to the unprovoked act of military aggression by the United States and Israel against the Islamic Republic of Iran," while pledging to urge Washington and Jerusalem "to immediately halt their unlawful and provocative actions," according to U.S. News.

item.title: Saudi, UAE leaders unite against Iran after missiles rock Gulf capitals
item.description:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Saturday to condemn Iranian missile strikes that rocked Gulf capitals from Abu Dhabi to Doha, in a show of solidarity that bridges a months-long rift between the two Gulf powers over Yemen.

During the call, the Saudi crown prince expressed the Kingdom's "full solidarity" with the UAE and pledged readiness to "place all its capabilities" at Abu Dhabi's disposal, according to the UAE's official news agency WAM. Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed expressed appreciation for Saudi Arabia's "firm stance" and "fraternal solidarity," and both leaders warned that the Iranian strikes constituted "a dangerous escalation that threatens regional security and undermines stability". They called for restraint and diplomatic solutions to preserve regional security.

item.title: Iran's defense chief, IRGC commander killed in US-Israeli strikes
item.description: Iranian Defense Minister Amir Nasirzadeh and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Gen. Mohammad Pakpour were killed in coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran Saturday morning, according to three sources cited by Reuters. The deaths represent the highest-profile casualties since the joint military operation — dubbed "Epic Fury" by the United States and "Lion's Roar" by Israel — began early Saturday with strikes across Tehran and other Iranian cities.

item.title: Israel locks down as Iran fires retaliatory missiles
item.description:
Air raid sirens blared across Israel on Saturday as Iranian ballistic missiles streaked toward the country in retaliation for a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, sending millions of civilians rushing to bomb shelters and fortified rooms in what became a nationwide lockdown.

Defense Minister Israel Katz declared a state of emergency across the country, warning the public of incoming Iranian missile and drone attacks. The Israel Defense Forces ordered all civilians to remain in protected spaces until further notice, stating that its air defense array was "detecting and intercepting threats". Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had launched a "first wave of large-scale missile and drone attacks" toward Israel in response to the strikes.

item.title: Gulf states condemn Iran after strikes hit US bases across region
item.description: World leaders scrambled to respond on Saturday as the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes on Iran, with governments from Moscow to Riyadh warning the offensive risks plunging the Middle East into a wider, uncontrollable conflict. The strikes, codenamed Operation Epic Fury by the Pentagon, prompted retaliatory Iranian missile attacks on U.S. military bases across the Persian Gulf, hitting targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Jordan — drawing a wave of condemnation and alarm from capitals worldwide.

item.title: FBI on high alert as U.S., Israel strike Iran
item.description:
FBI Director Kash Patel placed the bureau's counterterrorism and counterintelligence teams on high alert Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes on Iran in what the Pentagon has dubbed "Operation Epic Fury."

"FBI personnel are fully engaged on the situation overseas. Last night I instructed our Counterterrorism and intelligence teams to be on high alert and mobilize all assisting security assets needed," Patel wrote on X. "Our JTTFs throughout the country are working 24/7, as always, to address and disrupt any potential threats to the homeland."

The directive came as U.S. Central Command confirmed that strikes began at 1:15 a.m. ET on February 28, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps command facilities, air defense systems, missile launch sites, and military airfields across Iran.

item.title: Israel says Khamenei killed in joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran
item.description:
Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed Saturday in a massive joint U.S.-Israeli military operation targeting Tehran and cities across Iran, according to multiple Israeli officials. A senior Israeli official told Reuters that Khamenei's body had been found in the ruins of his compound. Israeli Ambassador to Washington Yechiel Leiter confirmed the killing to U.S. officials, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid.

The 86-year-old Khamenei, who had led the Islamic Republic since 1989, was struck in the opening salvo of the operation as Israeli and American forces simultaneously hit three separate gatherings of senior Iranian officials, an Israeli military official told reporters. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump were both shown an image of Khamenei's body recovered from his compound, Israel's Channel 12 reported.

item.title: Trump says Khamenei is dead after US-Israel strikes on Iran
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei had been killed in coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran, posting on Truth Social that "Khamenei, one of the most evil people in History, is dead". Iran has denied the claim, with its foreign minister calling the reports "mental warfare."

The announcement followed hours of uncertainty after the United States and Israel launched a sweeping military operation against Iran in the early hours of February 28, targeting military installations, air defenses, and government compounds across Tehran, Isfahan, Qom, and other cities. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a televised address that there were "growing signs" Khamenei had been killed when Israeli forces struck his compound in Tehran. Two senior Israeli officials subsequently told the Associated Press that Israel had confirmed his death and that his body had been recovered.

item.title: Israeli officials say strikes killed Iran’s senior commanders
item.description: Israeli forces killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei along with several of the country's most senior military and intelligence officials in a wave of "decapitation strikes" that opened a massive joint U.S.-Israeli military offensive on February 28, 2026, plunging Iran into an immediate succession crisis.

item.title: Trump backs regime change as Iran strikes continue
item.description:
President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday openly urged the Iranian people to overthrow their government, following a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and devastated military targets across the country.

In a video posted to Truth Social, Trump told Iranians, "When we are finished, take over your government. It will be yours to take. This will be probably your only chance for generations". He later called Khamenei's death "the single greatest opportunity for the Iranian people to reclaim their Country" and said that reports indicated many members of Iran's security forces were already seeking terms.

Netanyahu, in a nationally televised address, called on Iranians to "flood the streets and finish the job," describing the moment as a "once-in-a-generation opportunity" to dismantle the regime.

item.title: Pakistan rules out talks with Afghanistan as fighting enters third day
item.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan continued to exchange fire along their contested border on Saturday, with Islamabad ruling out negotiations and demanding Kabul end its alleged support for militant groups, as the most serious military confrontation between the two neighbors in years showed no signs of abating.

Pakistan's prime minister's spokesperson told Pakistani television on Saturday that "there won't be talks" and "there's no negotiation," insisting Afghanistan must first cease harboring militants. The statement came despite the Taliban government expressing willingness to resolve the crisis through dialogue. The European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also urged both nations Saturday to lower tensions, warning the violence could destabilize the wider region.

item.title: Airport deaths reported as Iran retaliates for US-Israeli strikes
item.description:
Coordinated military strikes by the United States and Israel against Iran on Saturday, February 28, brought commercial aviation across the Middle East to a near-standstill, stranding tens of thousands of travelers worldwide and forcing airlines from every continent to cancel, divert, or reroute flights.

At least eight countries — Iran, Israel, Iraq, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan, and the United Arab Emirates — closed their airspace in the hours following the strikes, which began around 1:15 a.m. EST. Flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed the skies over much of the region virtually empty of commercial traffic by Saturday afternoon. Preliminary data from aviation analytics firm Cirium, cited by Reuters, indicated that nearly 40 percent of flights to Dubai and a comparable share of flights to the wider region were cancelled on Saturday alone.

item.title: Regional toll mounts as Iran and Israel trade strikes through the day
item.description:
Iran launched waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel and multiple Gulf Arab nations on Saturday, hours after the United States and Israel began a joint military offensive against Iranian targets that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and struck military and nuclear sites across the country.

The Iranian counterattack targeted not only Israel but also US military bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Jordan, marking one of the broadest regional escalations in decades. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps vowed the strikes would continue "until the enemy is conclusively vanquished".

item.title: Iran forms temporary leadership council after Khamenei killed in US-Israeli strikes
item.description:
Iran has set in motion its constitutional succession process after state television confirmed that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed during coordinated US-Israeli airstrikes on Saturday, marking the most profound rupture in the Islamic Republic since its founding nearly five decades ago.

A temporary leadership council composed of President Masoud Pezeshkian, judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, and a jurist member of the Guardian Council — selected by the Expediency Discernment Council — has assumed the duties of the supreme leader, according to Iranian state news agency IRNA. Mohammad Mokhber, one of Khamenei's advisers, confirmed in a televised interview that the transition was being carried out under Article 111 of Iran's constitution, which governs the interim period following a supreme leader's death.

item.title: Iran faces leadership vacuum after Khamenei killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes
item.description:
The killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Saturday has plunged the Islamic Republic into its deepest leadership crisis since the 1979 revolution, with no clear successor and competing factions already maneuvering for power.

Iranian state television and the state-run IRNA news agency confirmed the 86-year-old's death early Sunday, following what President Donald Trump described as "major combat operations" launched alongside Israel against Iranian military and government targets. Trump called the moment "the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their Country".
